chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ibn Ri'ab from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): In

When a slave maraws a free woman and then is manumitted, and commits a major sin (zina), he said: 'He is not stoned until he has intercourse with a free woman after he has been manumitted.' I said: 'Does the free woman have the choice if he is manumitted?' He said: 'No, for she consented to him while he was a slave, so he remains upon his first marriage.'

key_terms.يُرْجَمُ: is stoned (punishment for married free persons committing zina)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave's marriage to a free woman if he is manumitted?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the specific conditions for *rajm* (stoning) in the context of a slave marrying a free woman, establishing that the penalty applies only if he commits adultery with a free woman after his manumission. The Imam further rules that the free wife retains her marital bond without the option of *khiyar* (choice) to dissolve it, as her consent was valid while he was a slave, reflecting the principle of *istibra* and continuity of contract in Shia jurisprudence.
